steps.title: One formula for every market
steps.text:
**Position size = money at risk ÷ loss per unit at the stop.**

Work out how much one share, lot or coin would lose if your stop were hit. Then divide the money you're willing to risk by that number.

steps.title: Shares
steps.text:
Account $10,000, risk 1% = **$100**.

Buy at $50 with a stop at $48: you'd lose **$2 per share**.

Size = $100 ÷ $2 = **50 shares**.

steps.question: You risk $150. You buy at $30 with a stop at $27. How many shares?

steps.title: Forex
steps.text:
On EUR/USD a standard **lot** is 100,000 euros, and a **1-pip** move (0.0001) is worth about **$10 per lot**.

Risk $100 with a 20-pip stop: one lot would lose 20 × $10 = $200.

Size = $100 ÷ $200 = **0.5 lots**.

steps.question: You risk $60 on EUR/USD with a 30-pip stop. A pip is worth $10 per lot. What size?

steps.title: Gold, indices and crypto
steps.text:
Same formula, different units. On gold, one lot is usually **100 ounces**, so a $1 move is $100 per lot. Index CFDs are often **$1 per point** per contract. With Bitcoin, a $1 move is $1 per coin.

Contract sizes vary between brokers, so always check.

steps.question: You risk $100 on gold, with your stop $5 below your entry. One lot is 100 ounces. What size?

steps.title: Always round down
steps.text:
Brokers have minimum steps: 0.01 lots, 1 share, 0.001 BTC. Always round **down**, so you never risk more than you planned.

The Practice and League screens do this maths for you. Now you know what they're doing.
